description.content:
Teel's partner-facing REST API. Partners authenticate with `sk_live_*`
(production) or `sk_test_*` (sandbox) bearer tokens issued by Teel.
See the [Authentication guide](https://docs.teel.finance/authentication)
for key issuance, rotation, and revocation.

**Conventions:**
- All endpoints accept and return JSON. Request bodies must set
  `Content-Type: application/json`.
- All money amounts use truncation (never rounding). Stablecoin
  precision is 6 dp; fiat is 2 dp.
- Write endpoints accept `Idempotency-Key: <8-255 url-safe chars>` for
  Stripe-style retry deduplication (24h window).
- List endpoints accept `?limit` and `?offset` for pagination. Limits
  are clamped to a per-endpoint maximum.
- Errors use `application/json` with `{ "code": "<CODE>", "error":
  "<message>" }`. The `code` is the stable, machine-readable identifier
  partners should switch on; `error` is human-readable and may change.


Contact Support:
 Name: Teel API team
 Email: api@teel.finance

Unauthenticated. Returns `200` and `{ "status": "ok", "env": "<APP_ENV>" }`
whenever the API process is running. Use this on the partner side to
distinguish a Teel-side outage from a partner-side credential bug.
Unauthenticated. Use for client codegen / Postman import.

Unauthenticated. The fiat currencies Teel supports, with the direction
each is available in, its amount bounds and its payout rails, plus the
stablecoin tokens and the networks they settle on. Derived from live

item.name: Lock a quote and execute a payout

description.content:
Lock-and-execute: this single call generates a quote from
`(fromCurrency, toCurrency, amount, recipientId)`, locks it, and
starts the payout. There is no separate `/quotes/*` → `/rfq/execute`
two-step. Pass `routeProtocol` from a `/quotes/*` response if you
want to pin a specific route token; otherwise the engine selects
the best route at lock time.

Scope: `payouts:write`. Idempotent via `Idempotency-Key`. The
response is wrapped in `{success, data}` — the partner-visible
payload sits on `data`.

A business whose payouts need approval is refused with 403
`APPROVAL_REQUIRED`: its payouts are created as drafts and approved
in the dashboard.

Optional. Stripe-style idempotency: same key + same body → cached
response replayed within 24h with `Idempotency-Replayed: true`.
Same key + different body → 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED. Concurrent
in-flight → 409 IDEMPOTENCY_REQUEST_IN_FLIGHT + Retry-After.

item.name: Lock and execute a batch of payouts

description.content:
Accepts a batch of payouts and answers **`202`** immediately. Nothing is
priced yet: locking each row's quote is provider I/O bounded by
per-provider rate limits, so it cannot fit inside a request and runs
after the response.

**Every row in this response is `pending` and carries no rate.** Poll
`GET /jobs/{jobId}` with the returned `batchId` for the locked rates and
each row's verdict, then `GET /payouts/batch/{batchId}/rows` for each
recipient's offramp-order result.

`batchId` doubles as the job id. `collectionId` is empty here — the server
creates the collection after this response — and arrives on the job poll.

A business whose payouts need approval is refused with 403
`APPROVAL_REQUIRED`, as on `/rfq/execute`.

A batch with a recipient the route's payout partner has not cleared
fails as a whole: `GET /jobs/{jobId}` answers `failureCode`
`RECIPIENT_VERIFICATION_PENDING` or `RECIPIENT_VERIFICATION_FAILED`,
and `error` names the recipient.

**From the collections wallet** (`userPaymentMethodId` is the
business's collections wallet): each row is sent as its own
stablecoin-to-fiat payout from the wallet, one row at a time, and
carries the batch's `batchId`. There is no collection and no
`GET /payouts/batch/{batchId}/rows` result: `GET /jobs/{jobId}` is the
whole answer, each row `accepted` with its `transactionId` or `failed`
with its `errorCode`. Every row needs `supportingDocumentFileId` (else
`422 SUPPORTING_DOCUMENT_REQUIRED`) and `amount`, the source its own
quote showed (else `400 INVALID_PARAMETER`); a row that now costs more
is sent at the price now when that is within the business's rate-move
tolerance, and otherwise fails `rate_moved`. A row the wallet cannot cover stops the batch:
it and every later row fail `collections_wallet_insufficient_balance`.
`onrampProtocol` is required but unused. A collections wallet held by
the business's owners is refused with `422
OWNER_HELD_WALLET_BATCH_UNSUPPORTED` before anything is created: a
teammate signs each send from it, so send that batch from the dashboard.

Scope: `payouts:write`. Send `Idempotency-Key` to make retries safe; a
replay returns this same `202`.

Optional. Stripe-style idempotency: same key + same body → cached
response replayed within 24h with `Idempotency-Replayed: true`.
Same key + different body → 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED. Concurrent
in-flight → 409 IDEMPOTENCY_REQUEST_IN_FLIGHT + Retry-After.

item.name: Get the progress of work accepted on an earlier request

description.content:
Some work is accepted on a request and finished after it, because it
cannot fit inside a request at all. This reports where it got to.

Today the only `kind` is `batch_lock`: `POST /rfq/execute-batch` answers
`202` with every row `pending` and no rates, because locking each row's
quote is provider I/O that does not fit a request. Poll this immediately
after submitting a batch.

**Poll on `terminal`, not on `phase`.** `phase` is specific to the
`kind` and its vocabulary may grow; `terminal` is true exactly when no
further progress will be made, whether the work succeeded or failed. A
client that reads `terminal` keeps working when new kinds are added.

`progress` is the kind's own payload. For `batch_lock` it is
`{rows: [...], collectionId?}` — one entry per item of the original
request, in that order, carrying `idx` so it aligns with your `items[]`
even when some rows fail. A row is `pending` (not yet priced), `accepted`
(priced, with `toAmount` and `effectiveRate`) or `failed` (with a stable
`errorCode`). `pending` is a real state, not a missing value — it is what
distinguishes a row still being worked from one that was refused.

For a batch's offramp-order outcome once the batch exists, use
`GET /payouts/batch/{batchId}/rows`. That endpoint covers the next half
of a batch's life and answers `404` while this one still reports
`batch_lock`.

Scope: `payouts:read`.

item.name: Get the offramp-creation outcome for each row of a batch

description.content:
`POST /rfq/execute-batch` answers `202` before each recipient's offramp
order has been created — that work is provider I/O and does not fit
inside a request. This reports where it got to.

`producer` is the batch-level state:

- `running` — not finished. Keep polling.
- `succeeded` — the surviving rows have offramp orders and the
  collection has been charged. Individual rows may still be `failed`;
  that is normal partial success, and the other recipients are paid.
- `failed` — the batch will not proceed. If it failed before the
  charge, nothing was taken.

`rows[]` is the per-recipient outcome, keyed by `transactionId` so it
joins against the `rows[]` returned by `/rfq/execute-batch`.
`hasOfframpOrder` is the evidence the order exists — status alone
cannot carry it, because a child sits at the same status before the
producer reaches it and after the order is made.

Scope: `payouts:read`.

Scope `payouts:read`. Returns the canonical, platform-level `paymentPurpose`
value set. The list is the SAME for every provider and route — each provider
maps a canonical value to its own API enum server-side — so this endpoint takes
no parameters and the response never reveals which provider will be used.

The list is static; fetch it once per session and cache it. Do NOT re-request it
per quote. Responses carry `Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600`.

Send one of these `value` strings as `paymentPurpose` on payout create/execute.
An unrecognised value is currently accepted and passed through to the provider
unchanged, but it will NOT match the provider's own purpose mapping and the
payment will be filed under that provider's default purpose — always send a
value from this list. `other` additionally requires `purposeDescription`
(10-255 characters).

**Deprecated.** Use
`GET /payouts/payment-purposes` instead.

item.name: Settle held balance to fiat or USDC

description.content:
Scope `settlements:write`. Moves money. `Idempotency-Key` is REQUIRED
and is held on the settlement itself rather than in a response cache:
a retry with the same key and the same `amount`, `targetFiatCurrency`,
`riskClass`, `recipientPaymentMethodId` and `payoutAddressId` returns
that settlement in its current status (with `Idempotency-Replayed:
true`) for as long as it exists; the same key with a different request
is `409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`. A settlement
that failed before moving anything is retried, not replayed.

Answers `202` with the settlement. A settlement still running after
about 20 seconds is answered early with its current status (`pending`
or `transferring`) — poll `GET /collections/receiving-accounts/offramps/{id}`.
If it has not been recorded yet the body is `{idempotencyKey, status:
pending}`: nothing has moved, and retrying with the same key returns
the settlement once it exists.

Allowed only when Teel can sign for the settlement wallet (custodial,
or a scoped settle signer on Tron). A wallet the business controls
must be settled from the dashboard: `409
SETTLEMENT_REQUIRES_DASHBOARD_AUTHORIZATION`, nothing moved.
(Required) Your name for this settle intent. Missing is `400 MISSING_PARAMETER`.
